scan.method: First dogfood run. One assistant session: web search (standard) per lane, primary pages opened where noted, GitHub repo metadata (stars, last push, latest release, archived flag, description) read from the GitHub REST API on 2026-10-30. Not an exhaustive market survey.
queries: Claude Code plugins marketplace official plugins 2026
Agent Skills open standard SKILL.md anthropics/skills repository
official MCP registry modelcontextprotocol servers popular GitHub MCP server Playwright MCP
background coding agents 2026 OpenAI Codex cloud Jules GitHub Copilot coding agent comparison
AI research search API comparison 2026 Exa Tavily Perplexity Sonar Parallel benchmark
n8n AI agent workflow automation 2026 release Zapier AI agents Make
trending open source AI agent tools GitHub 2026 aider OpenHands browser-use
Claude new features October 2026 release notes memory research
OpenAI ChatGPT release notes October 2026 new features
Zapier MCP server official docs actions AI clients
Gemini 3 release October 2026 Google Gemini app new features deep research
opened: GitHub REST API: repos and latest releases for every repo cited below

saturation.note: one to two query families per lane; lanes were not saturated. Treat each lane as a sample, not a census.

candidates.name: Anthropic Agent Skills (anthropics/skills)
candidates.job: ready-made Skills for documents (docx, xlsx, pptx, pdf) and a skill-creator for packaging repeated procedures
candidates.description: Public repository for Agent Skills: Anthropic's example and document skills plus templates.
candidates.evidence_notes: official repo and spec describe the capability; no independent measurement of output quality found
candidates.cost: free (repo); runs inside an existing assistant plan
candidates.privacy: skills run inside your assistant; bundled scripts execute locally
candidates.permissions: skills may run bundled scripts; review before installing (supply-chain risk noted by secondary sources)
candidates.reason: Document skills and skill-creator target two profile jobs (client documents, repeated admin); check on one real document against plain prompting first.
candidates.reverify_trigger: new document skill added or license change

candidates.name: Agent Skills open standard (agentskills.io)
candidates.job: write a Skill once and reuse it across skills-compatible agents
candidates.description: Open folder format (SKILL.md with name/description + optional scripts, references, assets) loaded by progressive disclosure.
candidates.evidence_notes: official spec; client adoption counts differ across secondary sources (20+ vs about 40)
candidates.reason: Matters only once you author your own skills; it keeps them portable between assistants.

candidates.name: Salesforce in Claude
candidates.job: pre-built sales skills over Salesforce data
candidates.description: Beta plugin with 37 pre-built sales skills for approved organizations.
candidates.reason: Profile has no Salesforce job.

candidates.name: Claude Code official plugin directory (claude-plugins-official)
candidates.job: add vetted code-review, security-guidance and language-server plugins to the coding agent
candidates.description: Official, Anthropic-managed directory of Claude Code plugins, registered in Claude Code by default.
candidates.evidence_notes: official docs; plugin counts differ by source (101 in March, 200+ in July, 250+ claimed in August)
candidates.cost: free with an existing Claude plan
candidates.privacy: plugins run in your coding agent with its permissions
candidates.reason: Profile reviews pull requests; try the code-review plugin on two real PRs against an unaided review.

candidates.name: Skill and plugin security scanning
candidates.job: scan third-party skills and plugins for malicious content on upload or edit
candidates.reason: Enterprise-only; not available on the profile's plans. Review skills by hand instead.

candidates.name: ChatGPT iCloud Mail and Calendar
candidates.job: connect iCloud mail and calendar to ChatGPT

sources.note: seen in search results; page not opened

candidates.reason: Profile uses Google Workspace, not iCloud.

candidates.name: GitHub MCP Server
candidates.job: let any MCP client read and act on GitHub issues, pull requests and code
candidates.description: GitHub's official MCP Server.
candidates.privacy: repository data passes through your assistant
candidates.permissions: GitHub token or OAuth scoped to chosen repos
candidates.reason: A terminal coding agent with the gh CLI already covers PR review; useful mainly for chat clients without a shell.

candidates.name: Playwright MCP
candidates.job: drive a real browser from the assistant using accessibility snapshots (no vision model)
candidates.description: Microsoft's Playwright MCP server.
candidates.privacy: pages visited are read into the assistant's context
candidates.reason: Strong tool, but no profile job needs browser automation yet.

candidates.name: Context7
candidates.job: feed current library documentation into coding prompts to reduce outdated-API errors
candidates.description: Context7 Platform: up-to-date docs for AI agents.
candidates.evidence_notes: README-level claims only; no measured comparison found in this scan
candidates.privacy: library names and queries sent to the Context7 service
candidates.reason: Profile builds Python tools; a one-week trial on real tasks would show whether stale-API mistakes drop.

candidates.name: Firecrawl MCP Server
candidates.job: search, scrape and crawl web pages into clean text for the assistant
candidates.description: Official Firecrawl MCP server: search, scrape, parse, crawl, map.
candidates.cost: UNKNOWN (paid API beyond free usage; price not verified)
candidates.privacy: URLs and pages processed by Firecrawl
candidates.reason: Built-in web fetch in owned assistants covers most reading; consider only for bulk crawling.

candidates.name: Official MCP Registry
candidates.job: discover and look up MCP servers with publisher namespace verification
candidates.description: A community driven registry service for MCP servers; reference instance at registry.modelcontextprotocol.io.
candidates.evidence_notes: listings are not vetted for trust (secondary review)
candidates.reason: A discovery source for this radar, not a capability to adopt.

candidates.name: Claude Duet
candidates.job: a proactive agent app that works on tasks on its own initiative
candidates.description: Research preview: a new app where Claude works as a proactive agent.
candidates.evidence_notes: one-line release note; product docs not read in this scan
candidates.reason: Already paid for in the profile's plan; try it on one weekly admin task before relying on it.

candidates.name: OpenAI Codex
candidates.job: background coding agent in a cloud sandbox, plus a terminal agent
candidates.description: Lightweight coding agent that runs in your terminal; cloud tasks from IDE, CLI or web.
candidates.cost: included with ChatGPT Plus (per secondary sources)
candidates.privacy: code runs in OpenAI cloud sandboxes for cloud tasks
candidates.reason: Already paid for, but duplicates the profile's coding agent; useful as a second opinion only.

candidates.name: GitHub Copilot coding agent
candidates.job: assign a GitHub issue and get a pull request back, run on GitHub Actions
candidates.reason: Duplicates the profile's coding agent and would add a subscription.

candidates.name: Hermes Agent
candidates.job: self-hosted persistent personal agent
candidates.description: The agent that grows with you (Nous Research).
candidates.evidence_notes: very high stars; no measured evidence of job improvement found
candidates.privacy: self-hosted; depends on configured model provider
candidates.reason: Popularity is not evidence; revisit when independent evaluations appear.

candidates.name: OpenHands
candidates.job: open-source autonomous coding agent in a sandbox (shell, browser, tests)
candidates.description: OpenHands: AI-Driven Development (formerly OpenDevin).
candidates.evidence_notes: SWE-bench Verified 72.8% cited by a secondary source; not checked against the leaderboard
candidates.privacy: self-hosted; code goes to the configured model provider
candidates.reason: Duplicates the profile's coding agent and adds API costs.

candidates.name: OpenHands (All-Hands-AI)
candidates.description: Same project under its former GitHub org; listed separately by some sources.

candidates.name: Aider
candidates.job: git-aware pair programming in the terminal with any model
candidates.description: aider is AI pair programming in your terminal.
candidates.maintenance_notes: last push 2026-05-22; latest release v0.86.0 on 2025-08-09
candidates.privacy: code goes to the configured model provider
candidates.reason: Duplicates the profile's coding agent; activity has slowed.

candidates.name: browser-use
candidates.job: let a Python script or agent drive a real browser (click, fill forms, read pages)
candidates.description: Open-source Python library for AI browser agents, plus a hosted cloud.
candidates.cost: free library; hosted cloud price UNKNOWN
candidates.privacy: pages and actions go to the configured model
candidates.reason: No profile job needs scripted browsing yet.

candidates.name: Gemini CLI
candidates.job: open-source terminal agent backed by Gemini models
candidates.description: An open-source AI agent that brings Gemini into your terminal.
candidates.privacy: prompts and code go to Google
candidates.reason: Third coding agent; worth a look only if the current one hits limits.

candidates.name: Cline
candidates.job: autonomous coding agent as IDE extension, CLI or SDK
candidates.description: Autonomous coding agent as an SDK, IDE extension, or CLI assistant.
candidates.privacy: code goes to the configured model provider
candidates.reason: Duplicates the profile's coding agent.

candidates.name: awesome-mcp-servers
candidates.job: curated list of MCP servers
candidates.description: A collection of MCP servers.
candidates.reason: A list, not a capability; the radar uses it as a discovery source only.

candidates.name: Claude 5.5 model family (Opus, Sonnet, Haiku 5.5)
candidates.job: current frontier, mid and small models for chat, coding and research
candidates.description: Opus 5.5 (Sep 22), Sonnet 5.5 (Sep 28) and Haiku 5.5 (Oct 7, 2026).
candidates.cost: included in Claude Pro (usage limits apply)
candidates.reason: Already in the owned plan; use the smaller model for routine work and the largest for hard steps. Nothing to buy.

candidates.name: Claude memory (Cowork and chat)
candidates.job: remember preferences and project context across chats and Cowork, with editable topics
candidates.privacy: stores remembered items; editable and deletable; sensitive-topics setting
candidates.reason: Free to switch on; review what it stores before using it with client work (profile privacy constraint).

candidates.name: Claude Cowork in any conversation
candidates.job: create designs, decks and documents from any chat
candidates.reason: Targets the client-document job at no extra cost; compare one real deliverable with the current workflow.

candidates.name: GPT-6 and GPT-6.1 Terra in ChatGPT
candidates.job: newer OpenAI models with interactive answers (charts, forms, task tools)

sources.note: seen in search results; page not opened

candidates.cost: UNKNOWN which plans include GPT-6.1 Terra (rolling out to ChatGPT Work and Codex)
candidates.reason: Arrives automatically where the plan includes it; nothing to change.

candidates.name: Gemini Deep Research Max
candidates.job: long autonomous research reports with MCP access to private sources
candidates.reason: Profile already owns two research modes; needs official docs and a head-to-head test first.

candidates.name: Perplexity Search API
candidates.job: raw web search results for agents and research tools
candidates.evidence_notes: BrowseComp 50-question sample, 2026-09-09: 74% at $275 per 1k questions (frontier tier), measured by a competitor; Artificial Analysis Search Index 80 per secondary sources
candidates.cost: pay per use; list price not verified
candidates.reason: Best measured accuracy-per-cost in the sources found, but only relevant if the profile builds its own research tool.

candidates.name: Parallel Search API
candidates.job: web search and deep research API for agents
candidates.evidence_notes: vendor's own BrowseComp run (bias disclosed): Advanced 74% at $399 per 1k, Fast 44% at $11.8 per 1k
candidates.cost: pay per use; tiers from about $12 to $612 per 1k BrowseComp questions including LLM tokens
candidates.reason: Same as other search APIs: relevant only for a self-built research tool.

candidates.name: Exa
candidates.job: neural web search and crawling for agents, also as an MCP server
candidates.cost: pay per use; list price not verified
candidates.reason: Measured below Perplexity at higher cost in the one benchmark found.

candidates.name: Tavily
candidates.job: search, extract, map and crawl API for agents
candidates.maintenance_notes: acquisition by Nebius in 2026 reported by a competitor; not verified
candidates.evidence_notes: BrowseComp (competitor-run) 66% at $935 per 1k; vendor claims first place on SealQA and SimpleQA
candidates.cost: pay per use; list price not verified
candidates.reason: Benchmarks disagree by who runs them; ownership change to confirm.

candidates.name: n8n
candidates.job: self-hostable visual workflow automation with AI agent steps
candidates.description: Fair-code workflow automation platform with native AI capabilities; self-host or cloud; 400+ integrations.
candidates.cost: free to self-host (fair-code license); cloud price not verified
candidates.privacy: self-hosted keeps data local; cloud processes data at n8n
candidates.reason: Directly targets the weekly-admin job; try one real workflow self-hosted within the one-hour setup budget.

candidates.name: Zapier MCP
candidates.job: let an assistant run actions in the apps already connected to a Zapier account
candidates.description: One MCP server per client at mcp.zapier.com; runs actions through existing Zapier app connections.
candidates.cost: uses the Zapier plan's task allowance (per secondary sources; not on the docs page opened)
candidates.privacy: actions run through Zapier and are logged in Zapier history
candidates.permissions: OAuth from the client, or a long-lived connection token (treat like a password)
candidates.reason: Fast path to assistant-triggered admin actions, but the profile has no Zapier plan; adding one competes with n8n (free self-hosted) under the one-subscription budget.

candidates.name: Make AI Agents
candidates.job: visual agent builder with a reasoning panel inside Make scenarios
candidates.reason: Comparable to n8n; no evidence it is better for this profile.

candidates.name: Activepieces
candidates.job: open-source automation with AI agents and hundreds of MCP servers
candidates.cost: free to self-host; cloud price UNKNOWN
candidates.reason: Open-source alternative to n8n; smaller and less evidenced.
